title: Randomized comparison of different reconstruction techniques for digital nerve coaptation
summary: Digital nerve (DN) injuries are the most common peripheral nerve lesions and are associated with high patient morbidity. DN injuries lead to a loss of sensitivity at the fingertip. To allow for sensory regeneration, surgical restoration of nerve continuity is needed. Most commonly, microsurgical suture-based nerve reconstruction is performed. Alternatively, tissue adhesives can be used. The aim of this study is to assess whether sensory nerve regeneration depends on the type of reconstruction.
conditions: Injury of nerves at wrist and hand level
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Complete DN injury of a digit
- Uni- or bilateral DN injury of a digit
- Single or multiple DN injuries
- Height of lesion: Lesion at / distal to A1 pulley
- Primary nerve suture (direct reconstruction or reconstruction with grafts/ nerve conduits)
Exclusion criteria:
- Incomplete DN lesions
- Secondary nerve reconstruction
- Pregnancy/ nursing period
- Diabetes mellitus, peripheral polyneuropathy or other neurological diseases interfering with nerve regeneration
- Known nerve compression syndrome of the upper extremity
- Previous surgery/ injury affecting the digit
- Patients under legal care 
- Minors (< 18 years)
